title: Accessible dialog
summary: A dependency-free modal structure with native focus, keyboard, and dismissal behavior.
overview: A small frontend pattern built around the native dialog element. It keeps behavior in the platform and leaves visual decisions to the consuming project.

sections.heading: Intent
sections.body: Prefer the native dialog element because it provides focus containment, Escape handling, and top-layer behavior without another package. Add Angular only for state and composition.

sections.heading: Minimal shape
sections.body: Keep the public API narrow: open, close, and a closed event. Project the body so the component remains content-agnostic.

sections.heading: Template anatomy
sections.body: Use a real dialog element and a form with method=dialog for controls that simply dismiss it. Keep the heading programmatically associated and let consumers project the main content.

sections.heading: Dismissal behavior
sections.body: Escape closes a modal dialog natively. If backdrop dismissal is part of the product behavior, close only when the dialog element itself is the pointer target so clicks inside the panel are ignored.

sections.heading: Accessibility checklist
sections.body: Give the dialog an accessible name, move focus to the most useful first control, restore focus to the trigger after closing, and never remove the visible focus indicator. Verify keyboard-only navigation and screen-reader announcements before reuse.
